acceptance: every element fits its container — nothing clips or overflows its box, and there is no element-level horizontal scrollbar
no horizontal page scroll — wide content (tables, code, diagrams, media) scrolls inside its own overflow-x:auto container, the body never scrolls sideways
text stays readable at every width — not truncated to nonsense, never below a legible size, no overlap between runs
images and illustrations stay discernible via max-width:100% + intrinsic sizing, not shrunk to an unreadable thumbnail
multi-column layouts reflow to stacked rows rather than scaling type or media below legibility to keep columns side by side
chrome — borders, padding, decorative frame — is never the majority of a block's visual mass, especially at the narrowest widths
no content is pushed off-edge or trapped behind sticky/fixed/overlay elements at any width
interactive targets keep an adequate hit area (~44px) at touch widths and never overlap or become unclickable
density and spacing come from the scale/tokens — no cavernous dead space when wide, no cramped collisions when narrow
empty / loading / error / placeholder states fill their area without overflow at every breakpoint
every breakpoint rule uses the project's breakpoint tokens/mixin, never a hardcoded magic-number width
every acceptance axis above was walked explicitly; an axis that does not apply is declared N/A, not silently omitted
